anatomy.intro: The drawing compares three foliage groups above one shared potting volume; it does not identify individual root connections.

parts.function: Overlapping fleshy leaves form the low Echeveria-type crown.
parts.label: Powdery rosette

parts.function: Sedum-type stems carry narrower leaves outward.
parts.label: Branching shoot

parts.function: Broad Kalanchoe-type leaves rise above their smaller neighbors.
parts.label: Upright paddle

parts.function: The same potting volume serves all components, so watering affects the whole arrangement.
parts.label: Shared medium

flowers.text: There is no single flower for this planter: Echeveria-type stalks, white sedum stars and paddle-kalanchoe flower spikes would belong to different components. None is documented here.

growth.note: Use photographs to watch for shade and crowding; these are possibilities, not dated predictions or instructions to separate healthy plants.

stages.text: Separate foliage groups fit together within the shallow planter.
stages.title: Small arrangement

stages.text: Stem extension, wider rosettes and taller paddles change the balance.
stages.title: Uneven expansion

stages.text: Offsets or flowering may develop independently in the different groups.
stages.title: Established display

habitat.text: This is a nursery composition rather than a natural plant community. Its working matches bring American Echeveria and Mexican coppertone sedum together with South African paddle kalanchoe. Similar fleshy foliage makes a pleasing display, but does not prove identical growth rates, final sizes or watering needs.

image.alt: Terracotta mixed-planter schematic with numbered pale rosette, copper stem, green paddle and shared medium.
image.prompt:
Create a square 1024px botanical educational illustration on warm ivory. Clean botanically accurate pen-and-watercolor, muted forest-green, sage and ochre palette, generous whitespace, large central specimen. Exactly four large numbered circular markers 1, 2, 3, 4 with thin clear noncrossing leader lines to the specified features. Numerals legible at 350px display. No title, words, paragraphs, watering icons, calendar, border or logo. Schematic anatomy, not a photograph of an owned plant. Show one shallow terracotta shared planter viewed slightly from above, containing pale powdery Echeveria rosettes at front left, narrow copper-orange Sedum rosettes on short branching stems at front right, and upright broad green red-edged Kalanchoe paddles behind them. Group types distinct, five small crowns total, not species proof. No roots, flowers or cutaway. Marker1 to a powdery Echeveria fleshy rosette leaf; marker2 to a copper Sedum branching stem; marker3 to a broad Kalanchoe paddle leaf; marker4 to the visible shared gritty potting-medium surface between them. All four leaders unambiguous.
Final refinement: Edit the supplied illustration. Preserve pot, plant arrangement, pale echeveria, copper sedum, all four numbered markers and leader lines. Change ONLY the margins of every broad green red-edged Kalanchoe paddle leaf at the back: they must be SMOOTH entire rounded edges, no scalloping, teeth or serrations. Keep red margins, broad oval paddle forms and everything else exactly as shown.

lookalikes.name: Lithops shared planter
lookalikes.text: Both share one pot history, but Lithops renew paired leaf bodies instead of extending ordinary leafy stems.

mature.text: The display changes as each component grows: paddle leaves can rise above the rosettes while sedum branches spread sideways. A small dish garden can gradually become a layered scene, with individual plants needing more room at different times.
